questions.title: Display Your Personal Information
questions.description: Write a Java program that displays your personal information in a formatted way. The program should print your name, your favorite programming language, and your goal for learning Java. Each piece of information should be on a separate line.
constraints: Use System.out.println() for each line of output
Include at least 3 lines of output
Use proper Java class and main method structure

examples.output:
Name: John Doe
Favorite Language: Java
Goal: Become a software developer

hints: Start with the class declaration: public class Solution
The main method signature is: public static void main(String[] args)
Use System.out.println() to print each line
questions.expectedOutput:
Name: Student
Favorite Language: Java
Goal: Learn programming

questions.title: ASCII Art Box
questions.topic: Creating, Compiling, and Executing a Java Program
questions.description: Write a Java program that prints a simple ASCII art box using asterisks (*). The box should be 5 characters wide and 3 lines tall. Use multiple println statements to create this pattern.
constraints: The box must be exactly 5 asterisks wide
The box must be exactly 3 lines tall
hints: First line: 5 asterisks in a row

questions.title: Program Documentation
questions.description: Write a well-documented Java program that calculates and displays the number of seconds in a day. Your program must include: a class-level comment explaining the program's purpose, comments for each step of the calculation, and meaningful output that shows the calculation.
constraints: Include a multi-line comment at the top explaining the program
Use single-line comments to explain each part of the calculation
Display the result with a descriptive message

examples.output:
Calculating seconds in a day:
Hours in a day: 24
Minutes in an hour: 60
Seconds in a minute: 60
Total seconds in a day: 86400

questions.title: Java Program Structure Analysis
questions.description: Write a Java program that demonstrates your understanding of Java program structure by printing a detailed explanation of each component. Your program should print: what a class is, what the main method does, and what System.out.println does. Format the output as a teaching guide.
constraints: Print at least 6 lines of educational content
Include section headers for each Java component
Use proper formatting with blank lines between sections

examples.output:
=== Java Program Structure Guide ===

CLASS:
A class is a container for Java code.

MAIN METHOD:
The main method is the entry point of the program.

SYSTEM.OUT.PRINTLN:
This statement prints text to the console.

hints: Use System.out.println("") to print blank lines
Think about what you learned about each component
Structure your output like a mini-tutorial

questions.title: Error Types Demonstration
questions.description: Write a Java program that prints an educational guide about the three types of programming errors: syntax errors, runtime errors, and logic errors. For each error type, print: the name, a brief description, and an example scenario. Make sure your program compiles and runs correctly!
constraints: Cover all three error types: syntax, runtime, and logic
Include a description and example for each type
Program must compile and run without errors

examples.output:
=== Programming Errors Guide ===

1. SYNTAX ERRORS
Description: Errors detected by the compiler
Example: Missing semicolon at end of statement

2. RUNTIME ERRORS
Description: Errors that occur during execution
Example: Dividing by zero

3. LOGIC ERRORS
Description: Program runs but produces wrong results
Example: Using wrong formula for calculation

hints: Syntax errors are caught at compile time
Runtime errors crash the program during execution
Logic errors are the hardest to find - the program runs but gives wrong answers
